artifact_schema.description: The discrete logarithm, as 64 lowercase hex characters.

k.description: k with k*G = Q, in [1, n), zero-padded to exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.

statement: Solve Certicom's ECCp-131, open since 1997: find k with k*P = Q on the 131-bit prime-order curve pinned in the checker. The parameters are Certicom's own, taken from the archived challenge page and authenticated by arithmetic rather than by their source -- p prime, curve non-singular, P and Q on it, n prime, nP = nQ = O -- so a corrupted digit could not have survived. THIS IS A FRONTIER OBJECTIVE AND IS NOT EXPECTED TO SETTLE. Pollard rho needs about 2^65 group operations, roughly 2,048x the ECCp-109 effort, which took 549 days across about 10,000 machines in 2002. It is posted because the network should carry an externally-defined benchmark whose difficulty nobody here chose, not because anyone expects to pay it out soon. Certicom's own prize is NOT claimable: BlackBerry retired the challenge and the pages are gone. This objective pays cairn's reward and nothing of Certicom's. Submit {"k"} as 64 lowercase hex characters, k in [1, n). See examples/certicom-ecdlp/README.md.
